finding: The four companies occupy different layers of the ecosystem: Tesla is a consumer Level 2 developer, Waymo is a Level 4 mobility operator, NVIDIA is a compute/software platform provider, and Mobileye is an OEM technology supplier.
By May 2025 Waymo reported more than 1,500 vehicles and more than 250,000 paid trips per week across four operating markets.
Waymo published matched benchmark results over 56.7 million rider-only miles, providing the strongest public exposure-aligned safety evidence among the four within the cutoff.
Tesla disclosed a primarily vision-based supervised approach, custom in-vehicle compute, fleet learning, and Cortex infrastructure.
NVIDIA offered a broad train-simulate-deploy platform and reference architecture, but direct vehicle incident rates cannot be attributed to the supplier.
Mobileye disclosed 29.0 million systems shipped in 2024 and technology in more than 200 million vehicles, but those units span mixed ADAS and autonomy tiers.
Tesla's simpler vehicle sensor bill favors manufacturing scale, while Waymo's redundancy favors Level 4 robustness within geofenced service areas at higher hardware and operational complexity.
Standardized cloud cost is driven primarily by GPU hours, experiment count, utilization, and price model; storage and transfer are secondary except for very large retained datasets.
Raw SGO incidents, California collisions, and disengagements cannot establish a universal winner without matched exposure, reporting threshold, ODD, geography, and system-version denominators.
Public data cannot support exact company training expenditure, private fleet utilization, sensor bill of materials, or unit economics.
